subject: Learning Methods
title: One Night of Lost Sleep
description: A 60-second lesson on One Night of Lost Sleep.

hook.text: After 24 hours without sleep, cognitive performance drops to the level of someone with a blood alcohol level of 0.10 %.

buildup.text: One night of sleep loss impairs attention, working memory, and the ability to form new long-term memories.

discovery.text: The hippocampus shows 40 % less activity after one night of total sleep deprivation.

twist.text: Sleep-deprived people don't realize how impaired they're. Self-assessed alertness barely drops as performance collapses.

climax.text: One Night of Lost Sleep matters because durable learning depends on method, not just effort.

punchline.text: One lost night drops you to legally drunk. Encoding collapses.

quiz.question: Why is self-assessed alertness unreliable after sleep deprivation?
options: Caffeine masks the subjective feeling of tiredness
People don't feel as impaired as they actually are cognitively
Alertness recovers faster than cognitive performance
